summary: User experienced API downtime due to expired token from failed auto-rotation, causing checkout failure. Agent restored service with emergency token, then negotiated partial compensation while preserving company policy. User accepted 20% credit and requested follow-up on script fix.

evaluation.reasoning: Agent immediately acknowledged urgency and apologized without defensiveness. Calmed user by focusing on rapid resolution and validating their business impact. Maintained respectful tone despite user’s aggression.

Agent correctly identified expired token as root cause and linked it to auto-rotation failure. Could have more clearly explained why auto-rotation failed or how to prevent recurrence during initial diagnosis.
Agent prioritized immediate restoration by offering emergency token before debating root cause. Action was swift, clear, and effective — service resumed within 60 seconds as promised.

Agent firmly upheld policy (no full refund for client-side issue) but offered escalating goodwill gestures (15% → 20% credit). Balanced revenue protection with customer retention by giving user a choice and closing the ticket amicably.

Technical cause was explained simply (expired token → 503). Next steps (emergency token delivery, 60-second recovery) were clear. Could have added brief instructions for token swap or script debugging in initial response.

strengths: Rapid de-escalation and immediate service restoration
Balanced policy enforcement with customer-centric compromise
improvements: Include brief troubleshooting steps or script debugging offer during initial diagnosis
Clarify why auto-rotation failed or how to validate it before offering compensation
